correctness.rationale: For 0≤j≤a the geometric sums satisfy sigma(p^j)|sigma(p^a) iff (j+1)|(a+1) by gcd(p^u−1,p^v−1)=p^gcd(u,v)−1. For each prime-power block choose d=p_i^j ∏_(k≠i)p_k^a_k; failures from distinct i are disjoint and count a_i+1−tau(a_i+1), proving bound. B=0 forces all a_i=1 and conversely all squarefree divisors have subproduct sigma. B=1 forces one exponent a=2 or3; exact cancellation makes d=p^(a−1)e bad iff M=σ(p^(a−1)) does not divide sigma(m/e). The unique unavoidable e=m gives n/p; excluding any other e forces M|q+1 for every q|m, conversely that suffices. Dirichlet gives infinitely many eligible cofactor primes, reciprocal-prime divergence in q≡1 mod M plus sum over large p of 1/p² yields zero density. Independently enumerated all 1≤n≤2500 and reproduced both fibers and unique bad divisor; finite checking not used to assert density/infinitude.
residual_risks: Higher B fibers not classified; density proof assumes classical divergence of reciprocal primes in fixed reduced residue class.
